0.content:
Diluc Ragnvindr is Kaeya's adoptive brother and the master of the Dawn Winery. As young knights they were Mondstadt's most eye-catching pair: Diluc the bright, elegant swordsman, Kaeya his friend, supporter and sounding board, "almost like twins". When Crepus died, Kaeya confessed his Khaenri'ahn origins to Diluc, they fought, and they have gone separate ways since. Diluc says you can trust half of what Kaeya says "at best". Kaeya says Diluc was cute as a lad but is no fun now, and mocks his love of grape juice. Kaeya worked out that Diluc is the Darknight Hero, set the knight Huffman to watch him as a test, then admitted he had watched the whole scheme and had "no interest in exposing secrets".

In Venti's story quest (1.0) Kaeya needles Diluc for selling off "Father's" mansion and asks after "a certain vase". In 3.1 (limited) he talked Diluc into supplying a barrel for Razor's festival wine and was pressed by Adelinde into staying for dinner. In 5.6 the two held a bridge during the monster siege. Diluc saved him from a Frostarm Lawachurl, insisting Kaeya was "in my way", and said he had seen through the trial because Kaeya was not "nervous" enough. In 6.4 they argued over whether Mondstadt is better guarded from outside the Knights (Diluc) or inside (Kaeya).

After their split Kaeya wrote to "D" with updates on the Eroch investigation, advice to leave Mondstadt quietly, three days' warning before an official Cavalry visit about the Darknight Hero, and repeated suggestions that the Darknight Hero team up with the Knights. Diluc answered tersely, told him to stop mentioning eyes, since he knew the right eye was not blinded, and to take better care of himself (Hidden Strife, 2.8, limited). In the manga Kaeya returned Diluc's discarded Vision disguised as a gift vase.

1.comment: Kaeya: Crepus and the Dawn Winery household
1.content:
Crepus Ragnvindr, the late master of the Dawn Winery, found the young Kaeya after his father left him and raised him as a son. Kaeya told Varka only that his father went to fetch grape juice "a decade ago" and never came back, and that he would not have survived that night's storm without Crepus. The narration calls this a carefully constructed lie: it leaves out his father's real farewell. Crepus died when the Delusion he used against Ursa the Drake backfired. Kaeya arrived moments too late.

The household still calls him "Master Kaeya". Adelinde, the head maid, looked after both boys as children. She remembers a gentle, polite child who did good deeds in secret and denied them, and says he will always be part of the family. Crepus once made Diluc scrub over a dozen wine barrels as punishment for a theft he had talked Kaeya into, and made Kaeya write lines. Kaeya then helped scrub until his hands were more bruised than Diluc's. Crepus understood, and mixed him a nearly alcohol-free drink he named "Cider Lake".

In his Hangout (3.8) Kaeya brought gifts back from Sumeru: a belt buckle for the steward Elzer, whom he sent to a doctor; hand oil for Adelinde, against chapped skin in the cold; and a decanter set for Connor. He helped old Tunner with the grape harvest as he had as a boy, and stood in for Elzer to host a Liyue Secure Transport Agency guard (opening the reserve collection). Tunner asked the Traveler to look after him, sensing "something deep-rooted" troubles him.

2.comment: Kaeya: Khaenri'ah and the Alberich Clan
2.content:
Kaeya's birth family is the Alberich Clan of Khaenri'ah, the underground nation destroyed in the cataclysm five hundred years ago. His father left him at the Dawn Winery, gripping his shoulders and telling him: "This is your chance. You are our last hope." His eyes held both hope and hatred. Kaeya grew up as a hidden agent, unsure which side he would choose if Khaenri'ah and Mondstadt went to war. He has since chosen Mondstadt and calls what remains of Khaenri'ah "sinners" not worth mentioning.

In 3.5 he said his life had less and less to do with Khaenri'ah as he grew up. He wonders whether his father left him there simply to keep him alive and cut off from "certain things". Dainsleif then told him the Alberichs founded the Abyss Order, and Kaeya said it confirmed an old suspicion.

A memento he hid (2.8, limited) says that the Alberich Clan, though not royal, stepped in as regents when "the one-eyed king Irmin" weakened. It urges the clan to blaze like fire, not wallow in the embers. Kaeya saved the page from a fire his father lit, against a clan rule that their affairs are never written down. He noted that it could never serve as identification and that he could not write in such a grieving hand "living in Mondstadt as I am". A wiki reading links the regency to the knight-marshal Anfortas and the Abyss Order to Chlothar. Canon has not shown how Kaeya descends from either.

3.content:
Kaeya met the Traveler after they fought off Stormterror and brought them to Jean. He cleared the Temple of the Wolf beside them and suggested they be made a knight. Soon after, he used them in a fake treasure hunt: he told them his pirate grandfather had hidden a magic sword from Celestia, knowing Paimon would spread the "secret" and lure the Treasure Hoarder Izzard into a trap. He apologised with the sword Harbinger of Dawn and promised not to use "the same method twice".

He now calls travelling with them perhaps the most fun he has had in his whole life. He sends letters, such as the one in 3.5 addressed to "next to a small, white-haired talking fairy", and is always inviting them for a drink. He insists theirs is not a transactional relationship. He jokes about their being underage for wine and points them to Mondstadt's apple cider vinegar.

In his Serenitea Pot he admits that chatting with them is "intoxicating" like drinking, and that they are the main ingredient in that cocktail. He offers to compile a guide of everything he knows about dealing with people. In his Hangout he drags them into spending his leftover travel budget, gives them a lamp said to have housed a Jinni, and passes some of the credit for his trip to them.

4.comment: Kaeya: Jean and the Knights of Favonius
4.content:
Kaeya is Jean's most trusted aide and the man usually wrapping up whatever goes wrong around Mondstadt. He tells others to give her their full support and jokes that she "positively terrifies" him. She trusts him but sometimes shakes her head at his methods, such as setting off a Ruin Guard to corner a bandit leader and putting his own men at risk. With Varka's expedition having taken the cavalry, Kaeya joked that he was a captain with no one to captain.

He says there are ten captains in the Knights and that not all of them can lead. He ran the entry exams that Mika took, and quietly supports Noelle at Jean's request. He organised a surprise day off for Jean in her story quest, then gave the Traveler all the credit, saying the closer you are to someone, the more bashful a surprise party makes you. On his Sumeru trip (3.8) he handed back his unused travel funds, after spending a day trying to talk the Traveler into helping him spend them.

In 5.6 he introduced himself as "Captain of the 9th Company" alongside Note (2nd), Skeiron (3rd) and Eula (4th). Varka says Feroux, then Diluc, then Kaeya held the Cavalry and that all performed impeccably; he plans to have Kaeya show the retired Feroux how far the company has come (6.4, limited event).

5.content:
Kaeya once told Varka that justice is a balance of strength and strategy, and that he shouldn't worry about the details. When Varka demanded to know his background, Kaeya gave only vague answers. Varka knows Crepus meant a great deal to him and that Kaeya stayed with the Knights after that injustice and helped expose Eroch: "Since he chose to trust us, I also choose to trust him." Kaeya regrets that no one in the Knights has inherited Varka's approach to work.

In 6.4 Varka's letter reached Kaeya at Angel's Share. Kaeya planned to report on public order, monster activity "and a review of the latest vintages". When the Knights wrote to bring Varka home, Kaeya's message was that he had a lot to tell him, but it could wait until Varka was back, and he promised an ice-cold drink.

6.content:
Rosaria of the Church of Favonius is Kaeya's drinking companion and trading partner in information. In 6.4 Eula said he was at Angel's Share "exchanging intel", with even odds he was just drinking. Rosaria says wine reveals true colours and she sees through Kaeya's smooth talk. Kaeya keeps her secrets and likes that she is honest with herself and does not fake interest. She counts the two of them among the people who are not "champions of justice to the core".

At the bar (2.5, limited event) she told the Traveler that Kaeya is only interested in people and things that intrigue him, and he complained she was saying too much. In 6.4 he asked whether she had ever actually been bound by the Church's rules; she said perhaps that was why she chose the Church over the Knights.

7.content:
Kaeya wrote Klee a "Favonius Survival Rulebook", gives her tips for slipping past Jean's investigations, and helps cover up her disasters. She thinks he is the best. During his Sumeru trip she believed he had been grounded too, apologised to Jean, and came to "rescue" him. He reads her The Fox in the Dandelion Sea, and says a childhood free of worry is "something truly precious".

In 3.8 (limited) Jean sent him with Klee and the Traveler to answer Alice's invitation to Sumeru's Veluriyam Mirage. There he and Klee acted in a play as a bandit and a mage. The outfit text has him gently fielding her endless questions afterward, because a child's curiosity should be treated with care. In 6.2 he shielded Klee when Durin's Abyssal power flared, and asked that she not be told yet what had happened to her friend.

8.comment: Kaeya: Dainsleif and the Destined Encounter
8.content:
In Chapter III Act VI (3.5), Kaeya was in Port Ormos on Knights business, studying Sumeru's spiced-liquor trade and talking to spice merchants. He had already tried every drink at Djafar Tavern. He told the Traveler about stowing away to Sumeru as a child. Dainsleif, who had been listening, called him "Kaeya Alberich... descendant of the Abyss Order's founder". Kaeya recognised Dain's eyes as those of a pure-blooded Khaenri'ahn, said the revelation explained why his father left him in Mondstadt, and promised to hunt the Abyss Order as gladly as ever. He invited Dain to stop eavesdropping and have a drink next time.

Dain told Kaeya that if he has let go of his past, he should keep it that way. After Kaeya left, Dain told the Traveler he did not yet know him well and doubted that anyone is truly unaffected by their ancestry. Paimon compared the pair to oil and water.

9.comment: Kaeya: The Vision Night and the Eyepatch
9.content:
On the rainy night of Crepus's death, Kaeya knocked on Diluc's door and told him the truth. They drew blades on each other. As his ice met Diluc's flame, a swirl of wind stunned them both and his Cryo Vision appeared. He never talks about where it came from. He sees it as a hard-won prize for telling the truth, and a reminder that he must live under the weight of his lies. The fight left a scar over his right eye.

His hidden note (2.8, limited) laughs that years of play-acting a one-eyed pirate ended with a real wounded eye. He says he never blamed Diluc, since he told the truth without expecting a fight, and that because Diluc believed he was blinded, he might as well keep it up. Diluc later wrote that he knew the eye was not blinded. Kaeya replied that not everyone in an eyepatch is blind, and some just have a scar.

10.comment: Kaeya: The Pirate Treasure and Kaeya's informants
10.content:
Kaeya's Story Quest (1.0): he invented a pirate grandfather and a Celestial sword in the "Lost Arcadian Ruins", planted riddles at the windmills and a waterfall, and had the informant Vile pass the Traveler a map. Paimon's chatter at the Adventurers' Guild carried the bait to the Treasure Hoarder Izzard. Kaeya's knights arrested his gang outside the ruin, and Kaeya and the Traveler saved Izzard from a Ruin Guard he had woken. Kaeya reminded Paimon she had wanted the treasure for herself.

Vile still works for him. Through her he once sent the Traveler to quietly free a woman from Treasure Hoarder blackmail, because the Knights would have exposed her past. At Lantern Rite (1.3, limited) he gave the Traveler a Treasure Hoarder contact, calling it "my own personal informant" and not Knights business. In his Hangout he told a grateful Liyue captain there are two kinds of people who owe him favours, friends and informants, then tossed a coin to decide and pocketed it without looking.

11.content: In 5.6 Albedo was tried for murder before the Knights and the Church, and the court appointed Kaeya to defend him. He pressed the prosecutor ("Hertha") on the missing bodies and the lack of a motive, questioned Diluc's dawn "stroll", and produced Sucrose as an alibi witness. When Albedo seemed to admit guilt, Kaeya asked the Traveler to investigate on their own while he worked on an appeal. The prosecutor was in fact an impostor. The plan to have the real Hertha "disappear" so the impostor would take her place was Kaeya's idea, and the news was spread through his and Hertha's subordinates. During the monster siege he fought beside Diluc at the gate and the bridge. Albedo thanked him: "good work, as always."

12.content: In 6.2 Kaeya played Genius Invokation TCG with the reborn Durin outside the Adventurers' Guild. After Durin got the exact same roll three times running, he joked that a god of fate could have cut the boy some slack, and that the cats at the Cat's Tail scratch him because he used to be a dragon. When Mondstadt suddenly forgot Durin and his Abyssal power surged, Kaeya shielded Klee, explained the situation to Jean, and agreed they should call Albedo home.

13.comment: Kaeya: Hangout Event - Shenanigans and Sweet Wine
13.content: Kaeya's Hangout (3.8): sent to Sumeru because Jean was worried about trade safety, he finished the job and was left with travel funds, which he tried to talk the Traveler into helping him spend. Depending on choices, he stood in as Prince Qubad for a desert troupe and improvised; spent the money on a trip to Liyue, where he and the Traveler swindled a conman with a rigged coin to recover a captain's money; or went home to Mondstadt. There he handed out souvenirs, helped Venti get Sister Grace's struggling amateur choir back on track, helped with the grape harvest, or ate Adelinde's steak. The endings return to the same themes: he would rather slip away than take credit, he believes people can leave the "script" they were handed, and the Dawn Winery remains home.

14.content: During the limited-time Hidden Strife event (2.8) the Traveler found a loose brick at the Knights' headquarters. Behind it was a box: the half-burned Alberich page, Kaeya's childhood eyepatch with his note about Diluc, two terse letters from "D", and a bag of faded seashells. The same event showed Kaeya's letters to Diluc kept at the winery. Treat the details as known only to Kaeya, Diluc and, if the scene allows, the Traveler.

15.content: Limited-time event appearances, canon but not universally known. Lantern Rite (1.3): identified the Treasure Hoarder symbol and set up an informant meeting, with the advice "wine begets wisdom". Invitation of Windblume (1.4). Midsummer Island Adventure (1.6): stranded on the Golden Apple Archipelago with Diluc, whose fire melted his ice paths; he later insists he "wasn't dead weight". Of Drink A-Dreaming (2.5): a Death After Noon at the bar. Of Ballads and Brews (3.1): fetched the Weinlesefest barrel from Diluc and remembered his father's farewell. Secret Summer Paradise (3.8): the Veluriyam Mirage. Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind (6.4): sparring with the adventurer Jack for a glass of wine, and reminiscing with Diluc in the memory bubble.

16.comment: Kaeya: Lohen and the Award Ceremony
16.content: In 6.6 Kaeya was organising the Knights' first award ceremony since the expedition returned, personally "quality checking" the celebration wine. Winfried, Leifhelm and Lohen were being honoured. He offered to make up the ceremony the Traveler never got for the Dvalin crisis. He predicted Lohen would be titled "the Benevolent Knight", get command of the 5th Company, and become the youngest captain, beating Diluc's record. Lohen says Kaeya can forge any captain's signature; Kaeya claims he does it only to approve his own leave requests.

17.comment: Kaeya: The manga and the Black Fire Incident
17.content: According to the official manga, set roughly a year before the Traveler arrived: Kaeya and Diluc turned down the Fatui officer Krupp's recruitment attempt. When mysterious black fires broke out, Kaeya first suspected Diluc because the power resembled the Ragnvindr Delusion, then found the real source, the girl Collei. He set out to kill her, but stopped when she accepted death and Amber arrived. He then enlisted Diluc, who posed as the culprit; Kaeya "arrested" him and handed him over to the Fatui to close the case. Afterward Kaeya returned Diluc's Vision disguised as a vase. Collei still dreads running into "the Cavalry Captain".

18.content: Mona calls Kaeya a Pavo Ocellus, "destined for greatness and grandeur" and for hiding ugly realities behind charm. She warns that he thinks he has made a clean break with his past, but one day fate will catch up with him and force a major decision. As of 7.1 this has not happened on-screen.
